name: example-mcp
description: Template connector for a hosted (remote) MCP server: registration, a reachability line, and the verb tiers an agent honors. Copy this directory, rename it, replace the placeholder URL, and list the server's real tools under verbs[]
surface: registration only (`toolbelt register example-mcp`, `--write` to merge into ~/.claude.json) — the server's tools appear in-session as mcp__example-mcp__<tool>; no belt code, no belt write path

origin.note: template authored in this kit; no code vendored. For a real connector, put the vendor's docs or repo URL in origin.repo

auth.flow: the MCP's own OAuth or device flow, driven by the MCP client at registration and first use; the server applies the operator's own identity and role to every call. The belt holds no credential
auth.login: toolbelt register example-mcp --write   (interactive; the client completes the server's OAuth on first use)
auth.note: Nothing is cached in this repo or by the belt. If the client stores the grant somewhere revocable, record the path, class, store, and revoke step here as an auth.caches[] entry so `toolbelt auth` can see it

verbs.name: search
verbs.note: template — replace with the server's real read tools; every read-tier mcp verb becomes an allow rule in the offered permission profile

verbs.name: create_item
verbs.note: runs under the operator's own grant at the hosted service with no belt gate (a connector has no code to gate in); the contract is the gate — preview the payload, get the human's explicit yes, run, re-read. Named on every doctor run by repo-integrity until a gated path replaces it

verbs.name: delete_item
verbs.note: irreversible at the service; denied in the offered permission profile, done in the vendor's UI by a human

risk.worst_case: create_item runs under the operator's own grant at the hosted server with no belt gate — the belt contributes registration and the tier list only; delete_item is tiered never and denied, so no reachable verb destroys data

safeguards: No local gate is claimed: the belt ships no code here, so it cannot enforce one. Whatever the hosted server lets the operator do, it does under the operator's own identity (SENSIBILITIES #13); the belt's contribution is registration, the verb tiers, and the permission profile derived from them (SENSIBILITIES #2).
Tiers are data, not prose: read verbs become allow rules, never verbs become deny rules in the offered profile, and an ungated write is named on every doctor run so it is never silently green.
The placeholder URL stays visibly fake until replaced; `mcp.registered` and `mcp.http_reachable` warn rather than fail so a fresh kit passes its doctor while still pointing at the gap.

mcp.note: PLACEHOLDER URL — replace with your server's MCP endpoint before `toolbelt register example-mcp --write`. For a stdio server use {"type": "stdio", "command": "...", "args": ["{TOOLBELT}/..."], "env": {}} instead; {TOOLBELT} and ~ are expanded at register time

checks.fix: Replace the placeholder url in connectors/example-mcp/toolbelt.json (mcp.registration.url and this check) with your server's endpoint; if the real endpoint is unreachable, connect your corporate VPN/ZTNA client
